en.title: Count Events in the Last 15 Minutes by User and Channel
en.description:
Process EVENT and COUNT in input order. COUNT u c t counts only previously processed events with the same user and channel whose timestamps lie in the closed interval [t−15,t]. Timestamps are not guaranteed to be increasing, and events that appear later in the input must not be counted early; duplicate events are counted individually.

The input and output were compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line contains q, followed by q lines EVENT user chat timestamp or COUNT user chat timestamp. This site uses 1≤q≤100000; user and chat are 1..20 ASCII letters, digits, or underscores; 0≤timestamp≤10⁹, in minutes.
en.output: First output the number of COUNT commands p, then output the p query answers in order, one per line. If there is no COUNT, output only 0.
en.explanation: In Example 1 the query results are 2, 1; the endpoint 15 minutes earlier is included. In Example 2 the timestamps are out of order and future times are not counted, giving 1, 1. In Example 3 later events do not affect earlier queries, giving 0, 1.
hints: First collect, sort, and deduplicate the EVENT times for each user and channel, and use a Fenwick tree to store the frequencies of processed events. Then process the input in order again: EVENT adds one, and COUNT queries the difference between the prefix frequencies for ≤t and <t−15.
